title: metadata-protocol: a second holder's declared .custom override is still judged against the first shipper only, for the sealed served-override types and the overlay list filter (ADR-0150 D4 follow-ups of #32613)
body:
triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

Filing gate: ① product defects with named locations, filed as one checklist card per #32997's follow-up rule (one closing card per landed PR, not one per item). Carried from #32613 / PR #33126 (review 6858448985, M1/S1/S2) by `epic:#31527#2` (6858471472). PR #33126 is scoped to the two types its card names (flow, action); this card holds the rest of the same ADR-0150 D4 step: **a second holder's declared override is served, judged against every shipper.**

## Checklist

- [ ] **1. The six sealed served-override types** (`servesSealedOverrideRow`: page, app, dataset, doc, book, mapping) still judge a declared override against `packagedArtifactOwner` alone, so the **second** holder's `.custom` override is declined. `dataset` and `mapping` are reachable today, since they have been per-namespace since #31700; `mapping`'s by-name read is the import door's. Judge them against every shipper (`someShipperOf`, as PR #33126 and PR #33129 do).
- [ ] **2. The env-wide list filter for the other overlay types** (dashboard, report, email template, …), where two packages ship a name and one serves a declared override. **Not measured on `main`.** Measure first, and fix only if it drops the second holder's override.
- [ ] **3. The action registry-reader face:** the hydrator registers an action override row under the bare name with the envelope `lookupArtifactItem` answers for the pair's id, while `getArtifactItem` falls to the first shipper's composite. `main` behaves the same (no regression), but nothing pins it. Add the pin, and the fix if the pin shows a wrong reader.

- [ ] **4. A declared App-pair row served at another package's address** (added by triage 2026-11-13 evening, measured by `epic:#31527#2` on #32561, comment 6863197549, on `main` and on PR #33148's head `72c8a9c8` alike). Module W depends on App A and on X and holds `de-DE`. `A.custom` stores a `de-DE` row declaring X, and X is refused at both the item door and the package door. Then `?package=W&member=de-DE` serves the row declared for X (stamped W), and W's list and execution list carry it, while the registry item at W is W's own and `overlayRowBinding` answers no package. `?package=X` refuses 409 naming W. The row is declared, so #33148 (undeclared pair rows) does not cover it. The save door and a cold boot were not probed. Same red-line-2 family as item 3: one package's address serves a row declared for another. Weight p3 (the wrong translation row is shown; rare configuration), so do it **last**.

- [ ] **5. A sole owner's exact address serves an undeclared App-pair row that its lists leave out** (added by triage 2026-11-13 evening; red-line read 6865563363 on PR #33148 / #32561 measured it on `main` and on head `dd283faf` alike, in both registration orders). Package X holds a name only through its own stored row in the bare slot, with no composite slot. Then `?package=X&member=de-DE` serves the App's undeclared pair row (bound to X as the sole owner), while X's list and execution list leave it out. This is a list-versus-exact-read disagreement, the class this card closes elsewhere. Weight p3 (rare shape; a translation row), done after item 4.

## Why it matters

An admin who customises the second-registered package's dataset or import mapping finds the customization declined, while the same act on the first package works. This needs two namespaces shipping one name.

## Reader

`domain:server`. ADR-0150's red lines apply. Pins should cover both registration orders, each holder disabled in turn, and one-holder controls, as PR #33126 does.

## Dedupe

`servesSealedOverrideRow`: 0 open. `second holder override declined`: #32613 / #32552 only (their own types). `packagedArtifactOwner`: 0 open.
